headline: Ghosts, Beaches, and *Beige Pop*
intro: This week's picks wander from Tate retrospectives and Venice premieres to AI anxieties and vanishing linguistic diversity in pop music. Also: libraries under siege, opera's data brokers, and the fight for public shoreline in Puerto Rico.

entries.title: James McNeill Whistler’s Music for the Eyes
entries.author: Olivia McEwan
entries.summary: A long-awaited Whistler retrospective at Tate Britain makes the case that every brushstroke, color, and omission serves the pursuit of harmony.

entries.title: Indispensable Presence: Ana Mendieta at Tate Modern
entries.author: Alison Hugill
entries.summary: by William Kherbek // Sept. 11, 2026 "Where is Ana Mendieta?" It is a question that has become familiar over the last decade. Jane Blocker’s 1999 book by that title is regarded as a critical point in the reassessment of Mendieta’s artistic legacy and subsequent understandings…[read on]

entries.title: Queen at Sea review – a harrowing vision of the future
entries.author: David Jenkins
entries.summary: Lance Hammer's long-awaited follow-up to Ballast is a harrowing yet vital tale of dementia, family and the limits of consent.

entries.title: VENECIA 2026. ‘BIOGRAFÍA DE JORGE LUIS BORGES’ DE MARIANO LLINÁS: LOS SENDEROS DE LA PALABRA
entries.author: Staff
entries.summary: Por Arnau Martín Un literato es su biblioteca; un autor, sus objetos. En Biografía de Jorge Luis Borges, una de las contribuciones más originales que han aterrizado este año en la Mostra de Venecia, Mariano Llinás convierte esta intuición en principio metodológico. Busca el espíritu del escritor no sólo en sus libros, sino también en sus cuadernos de apuntes, en sus fotografías y en aquellos…

entries.title: Pushkin and Putin
entries.author: Simon Garnett
entries.summary: The controversial reopening of the Russian Pavilion at the Venice Biennale, justified under the pretext of dialogue, legitimised the Russian state's weaponisation of culture – a practice rooted in Tsarist imperialism.

entries.title: Modern Pop and the Beigeification of Arabic Dialects

entries.summary: As Arabic pop returns to Arabic, Salma Mousa takes note of a new hybrid dialect emerging - one that risks flattening linguistic diversity. The post Modern Pop and the Beigeification of Arabic Dialects appeared first on Rolling Stone MENA.
